deepDive.title: Time zones — why your phone changes time on flights
deepDive.body: Class 7 mentions time zones. Class 8 makes them precise. Earth rotates 360° per 24 hours = 15° per hour. So every 15° of longitude EAST = +1 hour ahead. India sits at 82.5°E (Mirzapur meridian), giving IST = UTC+5:30. London (Greenwich, 0°): UTC+0. New York (74°W): UTC-5. Tokyo (139°E): UTC+9. INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE (180°E/W): crossing eastward = lose a day, westward = gain a day. So if you fly Delhi to Sydney (eastward), you 'lose' Sunday and arrive Monday. Major economies like China (3000 km wide) use just one time zone for political unity — sunrise at 8 AM in eastern Shanghai but 10 AM in western Xinjiang. India's choice of single time zone is similar political simplification.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11 covers solar time vs civil time + equation of time.

deepDive.title: Milankovitch cycles — why ice ages happen on schedule
deepDive.body: Class 7 says Earth's tilt causes seasons. Class 11 reveals THREE cycles vary over thousands of years — MILANKOVITCH CYCLES, named after Serbian mathematician Milutin Milanković (1920s). (1) AXIAL TILT varies between 22.1° and 24.5° over 41,000 years (today's 23.5° is mid-range). (2) ORBITAL ECCENTRICITY (orbit shape from nearly circular to mildly elliptical) varies over 100,000 years. (3) AXIAL PRECESSION (wobble of Earth's axis like a slowing top) over 26,000 years. Together these cycles affect HOW MUCH solar energy each hemisphere receives at each season. They're the master clock of ICE AGES — ice sheets advance and retreat with this rhythm over hundreds of thousands of years. Modern climate change is overlaid ON TOP of these natural cycles — much faster, human-caused.
deepDive.nextStepHint: NEET / Class 12 environmental science covers paleoclimatology and ice core data.

deepDive.title: Chronobiology — your body's circadian clock
deepDive.body: Class 7 says day-night affects life. CHRONOBIOLOGY (NEET-relevant) reveals every cell in your body has a 24-hour CIRCADIAN CLOCK — genes that turn on/off in a daily rhythm. The master clock sits in the SUPRACHIASMATIC NUCLEUS (SCN) of your brain — driven by light hitting your retina. SCN → controls melatonin (sleep hormone), cortisol (wake hormone), body temperature (~1°C swing), heart rate, gut motility. Disrupt the clock → jet lag, shift-worker disease, increased cancer risk. JEET LAG = clock misaligned with new sun. Melatonin supplements help reset. The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology went to Hall, Rosbash, Young for discovering the GENES that run this clock. Indian medical research studies pollution effects on circadian disruption — Delhi's evening light pollution shifts the clock backward.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Senior biology covers PERIOD and CLOCK genes — the molecular cogwheels of life's daily rhythm.
